w: A deer herd still grazes the parkland below this Elizabethan pile, built in the 1580s on a prominent hill in Wollaton Park. The house is now Nottingham's Natural History Museum, with the Industrial Museum tucked into the outbuildings, and the grounds double as a stage for rock concerts, sporting fixtures and festivals.
s: Elizabethan pile above a deer park, now two museums
_facts: Built 1580s on a hill in Wollaton Park
Deer herd still grazes the grounds
Now houses Nottingham's Natural History Museum, with the Industrial Museum in outbuildings
Grounds host rock concerts and festivals

w: Built into Castle Rock itself, with caves cut into the sandstone said to have brewed beer for Nottingham Castle since around 1067. The pub claims descent from 1189, though no document proves it - the current building dates from the 1650s, traded as an inn called The Pilgrim by 1751, and only took today's name in 1799.
s: Sandstone caves, castle brewhouse roots, disputed 1189 claim
_facts: Built against Castle Rock, joined to sandstone caves
Caves may have brewed beer for the castle from c.1067
Name 'Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem' first recorded in 1799

w: Nottingham's oldest parish church stands on High Pavement at the heart of the Lace Market, still known locally as St Mary's in the Lace Market. It's one of only five Grade I listed buildings in the whole city, and belongs to the Major Churches Network.
s: Oldest parish church in Nottingham, one of five Grade I sites
_facts: One of only five Grade I listed buildings in the city
Sits on High Pavement in the Lace Market district
Member of the Major Churches Network
